context_purpose: A subsidy or appliance-replacement programme must confirm the household is on the low-income or subsidised roll before granting benefits.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full bill with kWh usage history and payment record reveals occupancy and habits, far beyond roll membership.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The office still needs address and contact for delivery or payment, and cannot cross-check the account against the installation address from a bare membership proof.

transmission_check.reason: Household voluntarily hands over documents to receive a benefit, and nothing known obliges the programme to hold a bill copy, though programme-specific rules are unclear.

context_purpose: A subsidy body, processor or supplier assesses a merchant's sales volume to judge eligibility or creditworthiness.

norm_violation_today.reason: Per-transaction settlement lines expose customers' masked card data and purchase times, which the merchant has no reason to pass on.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Lender cannot see volatility inside months, refunds or chargebacks, or concentration of sales, unless these are added to the predicate.

transmission_check.reason: Private suppliers and processors ask for statements as a business practice, with no law known to require raw settlement records; government subsidies may instead rely on tax filings.

context_purpose: A pet hotel or shelter wants assurance that a customer or adopter has not been barred from keeping animals.

norm_violation_today.reason: ID photo and address are plausibly needed for contact and identification, so only the extra household and employment details clearly exceed the purpose.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Operators still need contact details and identity for the booking or adoption, and the ban register may not cover all past abuse.

transmission_check.reason: No known duty requires the operator to collect the ID copy for a ban check, so an absence proof could replace it, though an issuer attestation does not exist.

context_purpose: A landlord or shared-housing operator wants to reduce safety risk to co-residents before admitting an applicant.

norm_violation_today.reason: Private landlords are generally not entitled to sex-offender or protection-order status, and a full criminal record certificate over-discloses even where a police clearance is requested.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: An absence proof on two registers cannot cover other safety-relevant records, and it does not itself identify the applicant to the landlord.

transmission_check.reason: Whether landlords may lawfully ask for or receive such status at all is uncertain, so a minimal flow could be blocked on the question itself rather than on document format.

context_purpose: A promotion organizer wants one entry per real person to keep a prize draw fair and resist throwaway-number abuse.

norm_violation_today.reason: Collecting phone number, name, email and partial national ID for a simple draw entry over-collects relative to uniqueness checking.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Winners must still be identified and reached for prize delivery and tax withholding, and a per-person credential can fail if carriers issue per line.

transmission_check.reason: The retailer collects contact data for marketing and anti-abuse with no known duty to hold it at the entry stage, though winners' ID collection may be required.

context_purpose: A store applies a corporate-partner discount only to people who currently work at the partner company.

norm_violation_today.reason: Copying the badge and ID card collects national ID number and photo when only current employment at company X is needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Little: the store cannot tie the discount to a named person for later fraud follow-up, and the telco may still need ID when opening a contract line.

transmission_check.reason: The check exists to protect a discount scheme, with no known legal duty to keep the ID copy for this step, though a telco contract signup may carry its own ID obligations.

context_purpose: A nursing home or ward needs to keep infectious visitors and caregivers out during an outbreak to protect vulnerable residents.

norm_violation_today.reason: Showing or photographing the full lab report discloses diagnosis, values, medication and ID number when only a valid negative-window status is needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The facility cannot see test type or sample timing beyond the signed window, which only matters if its own policy differs from the hospital's.

transmission_check.reason: Outbreak access rules may name specific certificates or test types, and I cannot confirm whether a signed status would be accepted in place of the report.

context_purpose: A used-car dealer must be sure the seller can lawfully transfer the vehicle, meaning no seizure or transfer restriction applies.

norm_violation_today.reason: Household register transcripts with family members and address go well beyond what a seizure check and transfer form require.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The dealer still needs legal name and licence details for the contract and transfer form, so only the household-register and surplus copies are removed.

transmission_check.reason: The transfer process may require specific identity documents be submitted to the vehicle authority, and I cannot confirm whether dealers must keep copies.
